categories.main_business_segments: Shibusawa Logistics Corporation operates two main business segments: logistics and real estate. The logistics segment includes warehouse operations, port transportation, land transportation, and international freight forwarding, while the real estate segment focuses on the development, leasing, and management of office buildings and logistics facilities.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced logistics management systems, warehouse automation, and digital transformation (DX) initiatives to optimize operations. It employs both traditional and modern logistics methods, including modal shifts (rail/ferry), energy-efficient facilities, and robust information security (ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified) for trunk room services.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include manufacturers, distributors, and retailers, with a notable focus on beverage, pharmaceutical, medical device, and food industries. Major clients such as Suntory Logistics account for significant revenue, and the company also serves e-commerce and international trade sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company primarily operates in Japan, with a strong presence in major metropolitan areas (Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka, Nagoya, Kobe, Fukuoka). Internationally, it has subsidiaries and offices in Hong Kong, China (Shanghai, Guangzhou, Wuhan), Vietnam (Ho Chi Minh, Hanoi), and the Philippines, with recent expansion into Bangkok.
categories.supply_chain_position: Shibusawa Logistics is positioned as a midstream and downstream operator, providing integrated logistics services (warehousing, transportation, forwarding) and value-added processing, as well as real estate solutions for logistics and office needs.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening logistics service competitiveness, expanding outsourcing and value-added services, enhancing the real estate portfolio, and advancing ESG management. The company emphasizes sustainability (CO2 reduction, renewable energy), digital innovation, and human capital development, but does not conduct traditional R&D.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through service fees for logistics operations (storage, handling, transportation, forwarding) and rental income from real estate (office buildings, logistics facilities). Additional income comes from value-added services, facility management, and construction contracting.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other large Japanese logistics and warehouse companies such as Mitsui-Soko, Nippon Express, and Sumitomo Warehouse. Shibusawa Logistics positions itself as a value-added partner with a strong focus on integrated logistics and real estate solutions, aiming for category leadership in specialized logistics niches.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated revenue was ¥78.6 billion, with operating profit of ¥4.7 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥4.9 billion. The company has shown steady growth (7.1% revenue increase YoY), maintains a strong balance sheet (total assets ¥117.4 billion, equity ratio 54.8%), and employs 1,287 people (consolidated).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Shibusawa Logistics differentiates itself through integrated logistics and real estate solutions, a robust domestic and international network, and a commitment to sustainability and digital transformation. The company emphasizes reliability, safety, environmental responsibility, and the ability to provide tailored, value-added services that go beyond traditional logistics.
